reproduction_target: Comparative genomic characterisation of 22 Acinetobacter johnsonii isolates recovered from the NASA KSC-PHSF cleanroom (2007) plus one clinical carbapenem-resistant isolate (E154408A, Galway 2019), set against all 89 public non-MAG A. johnsonii genomes (n=112 total). Computational target: ONT read QC and assembly (FastQC v0.12 -> Canu v2.2 / Flye v2.9.1 -> dRep v3.4.5 representative selection); Illumina read filtering and assembly for E154408A (fastp v0.23.4 default settings -> Shovill v1.1.0); species-wide all-vs-all ANI cluster map (ANIclustermap) and per-strain typing (pairwise ANI against ANC 3681 GCA_000368805.1 and type strain CIP 64.6T GCA_000368045.1, dDDH via Genome-to-Genome Distance Calculator v3.0, BLASTN of gyrB and 16S rRNA); assembly QC (quast v5.3.0, checkM v1.2.3); annotation (Prokka v1.14.5); pangenome and core-genome definition (Roary v3.13.0, n=976 core genes); core-genome Maximum-Likelihood phylogeny (RAxML v8.2.13, GTRGAMMA, 1000 bootstraps, outgroup A. haemolyticus HW-2A GCA_003323815.1) with ETE toolkit visualisation; core-SNP clonality analysis (snipit, reference 2P07AA); functional annotation (eggNOG-mapper v2.1.12 with MMseqs search) and metabolic mapping into 232 KEGG maps (KEGGCharter v1.1.2); resistome / virulome / biocide-metal-resistome screening (ABRicate v1.0.0 against CARD 2023, VFDB 2022, BacMet v2.0 at >=80% identity and >=60% coverage) plus a custom ade-homologue database search; plasmidome reconstruction (MOB-suite / MOB-recon v3.1.9) and plasmid-borne ARG calling (ABRicate v1.0.0); and cleanroom abundance estimation from public shotgun metagenomes (fastp v0.22.0 -> MetaCompass v2.0 mapping to 2P07AA -> breadth-of-coverage with a 1000 bp contig cut-off). Isolate recovery and freezer-stock revival, ONT and Illumina library preparation and sequencing, MALDI-ToF species confirmation and disk-diffusion antimicrobial susceptibility testing are W (out of computational-reproduction scope).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis-invocation list built from the bioRxiv v1 JATS source XML. WebFetch was not used for the primary fetch: a direct curl with a browser User-Agent against https://www.biorxiv.org/content/early/2025/10/10/2025.10.09.681420.source.xml returned HTTP 200 / 142,591 bytes into the isolated directory /tmp/stage1_10.1101_2025.10.09.681420/paper.xml, and article identity was verified before scoring by grepping the title token 'Plasmidome, resistome' and the article-id 10.1101/2025.10.09.681420 out of the fetched file. The Methods section is complete in the XML (Samples collection; DNA sequencing and genome assembly; In vitro and in silico species typing; Genome annotation and phylogenomic analysis; Functional annotation of nucleic acid sequences and metabolic mapping; Species-wide characterization of the resistome, putative virulence associated genes, plasmidome, and antibacterial biocide and metal resistance genes profile; Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing; Estimating the abundance of A. johnsonii in NASA cleanrooms), as is the 'Resource availability' block. Scoring rules applied: (a) NO code repository is stated anywhere in the paper - the complete set of external xlink:href targets in the XML is bioRxiv-internal figure/table/PDF links, the CC BY-NC-ND licence URL, twelve author ORCID URLs, and four supplementary-file links; there is no GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Zenodo or Software Heritage identifier and no 'Code availability' section, so the Code axis is capped at 1 (reconstructable from prose) everywhere and drops to 0 for the three steps that are bespoke or tool-unnamed (C8 pairwise ANI, C23 custom ade database, C28 breadth-of-coverage). (b) The 'Resource availability' statement deposits GENOMES ('The genomes described in this project have been deposited at DDBJ/ENA/GenBank under the BioProject numbers PRJNA1128436 and PRJNA1209713') but never states that RAW READS were deposited and gives no per-isolate BioSample/SRA accession, so the six read-consuming steps C1-C6 score data = 1 while the genome-consuming steps score data = 2. (c) Three ABRicate invocations against three different databases are kept as separate steps (C20/C21/C22) because each consumes a distinct external reference database, and the plasmid-sequence rescreen (C25) is a fourth distinct invocation. (d) Version scoring: a prose pin counts as version = 1 when at least major.minor is given; ANIclustermap, BLASTN, the ETE toolkit and snipit carry no version at all and score 0. No lockfile, container image, conda environment, requirements file or release tag is claimed anywhere in the paper, so version is capped at 1 throughout and capture_claim is exact_pins_partial.

steps.label: Wet-lab: recovery of 22 A. johnsonii isolates from KSC-PHSF cleanroom environmental samples during (2P; 2007-06-27, n=5) and after (3P; 2007-08-01, n=17) Mars Phoenix lander assembly, plus clinical isolate E154408A from a rectal swab at Galway University Hospital (2019-03)
Wet-lab: Oxford Nanopore third-generation sequencing of the 22 PHSF-derived isolates (FLO-PRO114M flow cell, R10.4.1 chemistry; sequencing performed at KAUST Core Laboratories)
Wet-lab: Illumina MiSeq PE150 second-generation sequencing of A. johnsonii E154408A
Wet-lab: revival of 14 of the 22 PHSF isolates from 2007 freezer stock and purity/species confirmation by MALDI-ToF mass spectrometry (Bruker microflex)

Wet-lab: antimicrobial susceptibility testing of the 14 revived PHSF isolates and E154408A against 12 antimicrobials with E. coli ATCC 25922 and P. aeruginosa ATCC 27853 controls, incubated at 28-30 C, interpreted under CLSI M100-ED34:2024
FastQC v0.12 - quality control of raw ONT reads from the 22 PHSF isolates
Canu v2.2 - long-read genome assembly of the 22 PHSF isolates
Flye v2.9.1 - long-read genome assembly of the 22 PHSF isolates (parallel assembler to Canu)
dRep v3.4.5 - selection of the optimal representative assembly per genome from the Canu and Flye outputs
fastp v0.23.4 (default settings) - filtering of Illumina MiSeq reads for E154408A; 1,322,156 reads retained
Shovill v1.1.0 - short-read genome assembly of E154408A (assembly statistics reported in Table S1)

ANIclustermap - species-wide all-vs-all Average Nucleotide Identity cluster map over 112 genomes (89 NCBI RefSeq/GenBank A. johnsonii genomes after excluding 143 metagenome-assembled and 21 anomalous assemblies, plus the 22 PHSF isolates and E154408A); genome inventory given in Table S2

Pairwise ANI comparison of 3P2-tot-A and E154408A against the A. johnsonii reference genome ANC 3681 (GCA_000368805.1) and type strain CIP 64.6T (GCA_000368045.1) - Table 1; no ANI tool, algorithm or threshold named for this comparison
Genome-to-Genome Distance Calculator (GGDC) v3.0 - digital DNA-DNA hybridization of 3P2-tot-A and E154408A against ANC 3681 and CIP 64.6T (web service; formula/model not stated)

BLASTN - gyrB and 16S rRNA gene sequence identity of 3P2-tot-A and E154408A against the A. johnsonii reference genome and type strain (no BLAST+ version, no e-value/identity thresholds, no gene coordinate source)
quast v5.3.0 - assembly quality assessment of all assembled genomes
checkM v1.2.3 - completeness and contamination assessment of all assembled genomes (lineage workflow / marker set not stated)
Prokka v1.14.5 - structural and functional genome annotation of all 112 A. johnsonii genomes
Roary v3.13.0 - A. johnsonii pangenome construction and core-genome definition over 112 genomes (976 core genes; core-gene presence threshold and BLASTP identity cut-off not stated)

RAxML v8.2.13 - core-genome Maximum Likelihood phylogeny from the multi-sequence alignment of all 976 core genes, GTRGAMMA model, 1000 bootstraps, outgroup A. haemolyticus HW-2A (GCA_003323815.1); no random seed reported
ETE toolkit - phylogenetic tree manipulation, analysis and visualisation (Figure 1, including the per-terminal-branch ARG pie charts); no version, no script

snipit - core SNP analysis to assess clonality of the PHSF-originating isolates, using A. johnsonii 2P07AA as the earliest reference genome (40-77 core SNPs reported); no version, no alignment/variant-calling upstream stated

eggNOG-mapper v2.1.12 with MMseqs as the search step - functional annotation of all 112 genomes into KEGG Orthology, Enzyme Commission and COG categories (3,147 distinct genes annotated); eggNOG database version and MMseqs version not stated
KEGGCharter v1.1.2 - representation of the eggNOG-mapper annotations across 232 KEGG metabolic maps (Figure 2); KEGG release not stated
ABRicate v1.0.0 against CARD 2023 - antimicrobial resistance gene screening of all 112 genomes at >=80% sequence identity and >=60% coverage (62 species-wide ARGs)
ABRicate v1.0.0 against VFDB 2022 - virulence factor screening of all 112 genomes at >=80% identity and >=60% coverage
ABRicate v1.0.0 against BacMet v2.0 - antibacterial biocide and metal resistance gene screening of all 112 genomes at >=80% identity and >=60% coverage

Search of a CUSTOM database containing all ade efflux-pump homologues across Acinetobacter species; database contents, construction procedure, source accessions, search tool and thresholds are all unstated and the database is not deposited

MOB-suite v3.1.9 with the MOB-recon v3.1.9 sub-module - species-wide plasmidome reconstruction and typing across 112 genomes (89 distinct plasmids, 33 newly described); MOB-suite reference database version not stated

ABRicate v1.0.0 applied to the MOB-recon predicted plasmid sequences - identification of plasmid-borne ARGs (37 ARGs on plasmids in 35 genomes, Table S4), same >=80% identity / >=60% coverage thresholds

fastp v0.22.0 - quality control and filtering of public shotgun metagenomic reads from NASA cleanrooms (2016: 236 samples from JPL-SAF, 116 PMA-treated; 2018: 94 samples from JPL-SAF and KSC-PHSF, 24 PMA-treated and 23 untreated); NCBI BioProjects PRJNA1150505 and PRJNA641079; no parameters stated for this invocation

MetaCompass v2.0 - reference-guided mapping of the filtered 2016 and 2018 metagenomic reads to A. johnsonii 2P07AA (earliest PHSF reference genome) to estimate abundance and prevalence in JPL and KSC controlled environments

Breadth-of-coverage computation for PMA-treated and untreated samples from 2016 and 2018 from the fraction of reads mapped to the reference genome, with a contig length cut-off score of 1000 bp; no tool, script or explicit formula given for the fraction-to-breadth conversion

headline.static_readiness: 0/28 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification). Under-claims by construction: Tier-1 cannot credit an undeclared-but-present dependency capture.
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 21/28 (75%) RI, 7/28 (25%) NI, 0 X. This paper is an unusually clean example of the dominant genomics-survey pattern: near-complete per-tool version pinning in prose, near-complete public data deposition, and ZERO analysis code. Twenty of the twenty-eight computational steps are single invocations of a named, exactly-pinned, publicly available tool (FastQC v0.12, Canu v2.2, Flye v2.9.1, dRep v3.4.5, fastp v0.23.4 and v0.22.0, Shovill v1.1.0, GGDC v3.0, quast v5.3.0, checkM v1.2.3, Prokka v1.14.5, Roary v3.13.0, RAxML v8.2.13, eggNOG-mapper v2.1.12, KEGGCharter v1.1.2, ABRicate v1.0.0, MOB-suite/MOB-recon v3.1.9, MetaCompass v2.0), which is why the RI fraction is high. The seven NI steps fall into two groups: four unversioned tools (C7 ANIclustermap, C10 BLASTN, C16 ETE toolkit, C17 snipit) and three steps with no identifiable executable at all (C8 the pairwise ANI behind Table 1, C23 the custom ade-homologue database search, C28 the breadth-of-coverage computation behind the cleanroom abundance claim). C23 is the worst single step: the database is custom, undeposited, and its composition, source accessions, search tool and thresholds are all unstated, so the Ade efflux-pump result cannot be re-derived at all. The Code axis is capped at 1 for every step because the paper contains no code repository of any kind - no GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Zenodo or Software Heritage identifier appears anywhere in the article XML, and there is no 'Code availability' section. Version is capped at 1 for every step because no lockfile, container image or digest, conda environment file or requirements file is claimed anywhere, so even a successful stage-2 code check could not lift any step to R-star; capture_claim is exact_pins_partial and stage2_candidate is false.
headline.coverage: 28 computational steps enumerated from the Methods sections 'DNA sequencing and genome assembly', 'In vitro and in silico species typing', 'Genome annotation and phylogenomic analysis', 'Functional annotation of nucleic acid sequences and metabolic mapping', 'Species-wide characterization of the resistome, putative virulence associated genes, plasmidome, and antibacterial biocide and metal resistance genes profile', and 'Estimating the abundance of A. johnsonii in NASA cleanrooms'. 5 coarse wet-lab steps (isolate recovery, ONT sequencing, Illumina sequencing, freezer-stock revival plus MALDI-ToF, disk-diffusion AST) counted in W and out of computational-reproduction scope. Coverage = 28/33 (85%) of enumerated steps are C-layer.

gaps.missing: The paper deposits no analysis code and makes no statement about code at all. There is no 'Code availability' section; the 'Resource availability' block consists of exactly one bullet, quoted verbatim: 'The genomes described in this project have been deposited at DDBJ/ENA/GenBank under the BioProject numbers PRJNA1128436 and PRJNA1209713.' The complete set of external xlink:href targets in the article XML is bioRxiv-internal figure/table/PDF links, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/, twelve author ORCID URLs, and four supplementary-file links (681420_file03.pdf, 681420_file04.xlsx, 681420_file05.xlsx, 681420_file06.xlsx) - no GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Zenodo or Software Heritage identifier appears anywhere. Absence of a repository is recorded here as the finding; no web search was performed to locate one. Consequently no driver script, no parameter file, no assembler command line, no dRep selection criteria, no Roary configuration, no RAxML invocation, no eggNOG-mapper command, no plotting code for Figures 1-5, and no breadth-of-coverage code exists in any retrievable form.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the analysis as a public repository with a tagged release archived to Zenodo: the assembly driver (Canu and Flye command lines including genomeSize and read-type flags), the dRep selection configuration, the Roary and RAxML invocations with seeds, the eggNOG-mapper and KEGGCharter commands, the ABRicate wrapper and its database provisioning, the MOB-recon invocation, the MetaCompass configuration, the breadth-of-coverage script, and the ETE toolkit figure code. None of this carries any data-sensitivity risk.

gaps.where: Newly generated sequencing data - steps C1-C6 (raw ONT and Illumina reads for the 22 PHSF isolates and E154408A)
gaps.missing: The deposition statement covers GENOMES only ('The genomes described in this project have been deposited at DDBJ/ENA/GenBank under the BioProject numbers PRJNA1128436 and PRJNA1209713') and never states that the raw reads were submitted to SRA/ENA. No BioSample accession, no SRA run accession, and no per-isolate accession table is given for any of the 23 newly sequenced strains, so there is no documented mapping from the isolate names used throughout the paper (2P07AA, 2P08AD, 3P2-tot-A, 3P06AC, E154408A, and the remaining 18) to a retrievable record. Which of the two BioProjects holds the cleanroom isolates and which holds the clinical isolate is also not stated. Steps C1-C6 (FastQC, Canu, Flye, dRep, fastp, Shovill) therefore cannot be entered with certainty and score data = 1.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a per-isolate accession table (isolate name -> BioSample -> SRA run -> assembly accession) as a supplementary table, state explicitly that the raw ONT and Illumina reads are deposited, and say which BioProject covers which sample set.

gaps.where: Whole analysis environment - all 28 computational steps
gaps.missing: No environment capture of any kind is claimed. There is no lockfile (conda-lock, renv.lock, pixi.lock), no container image or digest, no conda/mamba environment.yml, no requirements.txt, no Nextflow/Snakemake configuration, and no statement of the operating system, Python version, Perl version or R version underlying the stack. The stack spans command-line C/C++ tools (Canu, Flye, quast, RAxML, MMseqs, BLASTN), Python (checkM, dRep, KEGGCharter, ANIclustermap, ETE toolkit, snipit, MOB-suite), Perl (Prokka, ABRicate, Roary, Shovill) and an external web service (GGDC), with no dependency closure captured for any of them. This is precisely why capture_claim is exact_pins_partial rather than env_lock_claimed despite the otherwise thorough per-tool pinning, and why version is capped at 1 for every step.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a conda-lock or container digest covering the full command-line/Python/Perl stack for a declared platform, and cite it from the availability statement. Given that every tool already carries an exact version in prose, generating a lock is close to mechanical.

gaps.where: C23 - custom ade efflux-pump homologue database
gaps.missing: Verbatim: 'A custom database containing all ade homologues across Acinetobacter species was used to search for Ade efflux-pump-encoding genes.' Nothing else is given. The database is not deposited, its source accessions and the Acinetobacter species included are not listed, the sequence set (nucleotide or protein) is not specified, no construction procedure or curation date is described, the search tool is not named (ABRicate is implied by context but not stated), and no identity or coverage thresholds are given for this search. The Ade efflux-pump results reported for the PHSF isolates and E154408A therefore cannot be re-derived by any route.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the custom ade database as a supplementary FASTA with a checksum and an accession list, state the tool and thresholds used against it, and record the date and source release from which the homologues were harvested.

gaps.where: External reference databases - C12 (checkM marker set), C13 (Prokka databases), C18 (eggNOG database), C19 (KEGG), C20 (CARD), C21 (VFDB), C22 (BacMet), C24 (MOB-suite reference database)
gaps.missing: Every database is obtained out of band, and pinning is uneven. Three are dated or versioned in prose - CARD 2023, VFDB 2022, BacMet v2.0 - but with no download date, no release identifier, no URL and no checksum. Five carry no version information at all: the checkM marker set / lineage workflow, the Prokka annotation databases, the eggNOG database release behind eggNOG-mapper v2.1.12, the KEGG release behind the 232 KEGGCharter maps, and the MOB-suite reference plasmid database behind MOB-recon v3.1.9. CARD, VFDB, BacMet, eggNOG, KEGG and the MOB-suite database are all rolling resources, so gene-content counts (62 species-wide ARGs, 89 predicted plasmids, 3,147 annotated genes) are not recoverable without the exact release. Under the Stage-2 taxonomy these would be at best class B (pin in prose only) and several would be class C (mutable latest); at Stage 1 env_capture_class is left n/a per protocol.
gaps.how_to_close: Record the exact release identifier, download URL and download date (ideally a checksum) for every reference database, and provide a fetch script that pins each artifact to a versioned URL or DOI rather than relying on whatever the tool downloads at install time.

gaps.where: C15 - RAxML v8.2.13 core-genome ML phylogeny, and by inheritance C16 (tree visualisation) and the clade assignments in the Results
gaps.missing: No random seed is reported anywhere in the paper. RAxML requires a parsimony starting seed (-p) and, for rapid bootstrapping, a bootstrap seed (-x); both are omitted. The 1000-bootstrap support values and, at 40-77 core SNPs of divergence within the PHSF clade, the fine topology of the monophyletic PHSF cluster and its placement relative to strain M19 are therefore reproducible only distributionally, not exactly. The upstream core-gene alignment is also not deposited, so a re-run starts from a re-derived alignment rather than the authors' own.
gaps.how_to_close: Report the RAxML seeds, deposit the 976-core-gene concatenated alignment and the resulting Newick tree with bootstrap values as supplementary files, and state the RAxML executable variant used (raxmlHPC-PTHREADS and thread count).

gaps.where: C9 - digital DNA-DNA hybridization via the Genome-to-Genome Distance Calculator v3.0 web service
gaps.missing: The dDDH values in Table 1 (65.60% and 66.20% for 3P2-tot-A; the analogous values for E154408A) are produced by an external web server rather than by locally executed code. The GGDC formula is not stated (GGDC reports three formulas, d0/d4/d6, with different recommended uses), the query and reference submission dates are not given, and the underlying BLAST+ backend version used by the server at the time of submission is not recorded. The server is versioned as v3.0 but is a moving service outside the authors' control, so the exact numbers are not re-derivable if the server is upgraded or retired.
gaps.how_to_close: State which GGDC formula was used, record the submission date and the result identifier returned by the server, and attach the full GGDC result output as supplementary data so the reported values remain checkable independent of the service.

gaps.where: C7 (ANIclustermap), C8 (pairwise ANI), C10 (BLASTN), C16 (ETE toolkit), C17 (snipit), C28 (breadth of coverage)
gaps.missing: Version pinning is dense and exact across most of the paper but absent for six steps. ANIclustermap, the ETE toolkit and snipit are named without any version; BLASTN is named without a BLAST+ version, e-value, or identity/coverage threshold; the pairwise ANI behind Table 1 names no tool at all (fastANI, OrthoANI, ANIb and pyani give measurably different values, so the reported 95.90% / 95.83% cannot be checked); and the breadth-of-coverage computation in C28 names neither a tool nor an explicit formula, stating only that 'the fraction of mapped reads to the reference genome was used to calculate the corresponding breadth of coverage' with 'a contig length cut-off score of 1000 bp'. C28 carries the paper's cleanroom-abundance conclusion, so this omission is load-bearing rather than cosmetic.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a software table with an exact version (and git commit where a tool is used from a repository rather than a release) for every tool including ANIclustermap, BLAST+, ETE, snipit and MetaCompass; name the ANI implementation and threshold used for Table 1; and write out the breadth-of-coverage definition explicitly (mapped base positions over reference length, or whatever was actually computed) alongside the script that computes it.
